- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00 or negative), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., recent prices falling from 90+ to 70s), model overreacts to recent lows; apply upward bias to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.20), model often underestimates upside; increase forecast by 3–7% for 30-day horizon, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast) — apply slight upward adjustment for first 3–5 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is stable or flat, model often fails to capture long-term trend; use 30-day moving average of history as baseline for correction.
- Overshoots after spikes are common in model’s 30-day forecast — apply “clipping” rule: cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high if sentiment is neutral or positive.
